title: Æbleskiver: Danish Pancake Puffs with a Cinnamon Apple Centre
summary: Fluffy pancake balls with a soft cinnamon apple centre, turned golden in an æbleskiver pan and served with berry jam.
equipment: 2 wooden skewers or a knitting needle

ingredients.item: medium eating apple (about 150 g), peeled, cored and cut into 5 mm dice
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the apple
steps.text: Melt the 15 g butter in the small frying pan and add the diced apple, brown sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice. Cook over medium heat for 6-8 min, stirring, until tender and coated in a light syrup, then leave to cool.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon and salt together in a bowl.

steps.title: Add the wet ingredients
steps.text: Beat the egg yolks with the milk, melted butter and vanilla, then whisk into the dry mix until just smooth. A few small lumps are fine.

steps.title: Fold in the whites
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl to soft peaks and fold them into the batter in two additions, keeping as much air as possible. This makes the balls light and puffy.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Warm the æbleskiver pan over medium-low heat for 3-4 min, then brush each hollow generously with butter.

steps.title: Fill the hollows
steps.text: Spoon about 1 tbsp batter into each hollow, add a teaspoon of apple, and cover with another tablespoon of batter so each hollow is nearly full.

steps.title: Turn into balls
steps.text: After 3-4 min, when the undersides are golden, use the skewers to turn each one a quarter turn so the uncooked batter flows into the hollow. Keep turning every minute or so for about 3 min more, until they are round and golden all over and a skewer comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Cook the remaining batter the same way, buttering the pan between batches. Dust with icing sugar and serve hot with the jam for dipping.

tips: A common mistake is a pan that is too hot: the outside burns before the centre sets. Medium-low heat is enough.
Keep the apple pieces small so the balls close neatly around them.
Turn early and often for the roundest shape.
A knitting needle or wooden skewer works better than a fork for turning.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Cool leftovers, keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days and warm in a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven for 5-8 min.
